analysis.title: US Market Intelligence Afternoon Briefing, October 26, 2026
key_insights: US stocks closed higher but off best levels on Oct 26: SPX +0.7%, NDX +1.1%, RTY +0.4%. SPW lagged SPX on AI-trade leadership. SOXX +2.9% and DRAM +2.7% on AI capex and financing headlines.

AI financing headlines drove semis: META announced a $95bn equity raise with NVDA, AMD and AVGO indicating interest in buying up to $5bn of it, SPCX closed a $40bn chip financing deal with APO, and AWS said 2026 cloud capacity is sold out with most large 2027 blocks booked.

JPM says the focus stays on the cost and availability of AI capital. This week's Mag 7 earnings need to support the sustainability of AI financing and hyperscaler capex for investors to gain conviction in tech.
Positioning in AI Core Revenue and Semis has fallen to the 94th percentile long-term from the 99th, but has not fully cleared.

Oil pulled back from a one-month high (WTI settled near $103 per the narrative, Brent ~$112) as the market took Trump's 'no immediate action' comments on Iran positively. Trump said he will soon decide whether to make a deal or 'finish it off', and there is little sign of progress toward a deal.

JPM US Market Intel view: remains Tactically Bullish. SPX lost 2.4% over the last two weeks with a shift to defensives, and is -36bp MTD. Basis is economy growing at or above trend, Flash PMIs pointing to ~5% annualized real growth, and about a quarter of SPX reported with no dips to pre-season forecasts (~13% revenue growth, ~30% EPS growth, ~15% margins).
JPM says the signal is less clear because there has not been a complete positioning washout despite sentiment in the Fear region.

If Trump moves back to negotiations rather than kinetics on Iran, JPM expects a broad rally led by Tech and Cyclicals ex-Energy. Iran has said any new bombing would lead it to target the region including Israel and the UAE, which JPM calls a key risk.

Monetization Menu: the prior menu aligns with the view, and JPM would consider adding hedges via longs in oil / Energy equities and long vol. The Oct 19 menu retained a preference for Tech via pairs trades and derivatives, constructive on Financials and Retailers, and favored Brazil and Japan.
EWZ finished down 20% after the Brazil election runoff. ETF desk (Rogerson) expected to stay active in EWZ, EWZS, FLBR and ILF and noted net adds from RM customers in recent weeks.

Europe closed higher led by Italy: UKX +0.7%, SX5E +0.8%, DAX +0.9%. French OATs tightened ~13bp after Moody's kept France at Aa3 with a negative outlook, and the 10Y OAT fell below 4.9% after touching 5% last week for the first time since 2002.
German IFO improved for a sixth straight month to 90.2 vs 89.8 survey and 89.9 prior. Fed, ECB and BoJ decisions are all expected on hold, and the UK Budget is Wednesday.

Consumer desk (Barton): mixed tape with little evidence of rotation. Specialty retail (URBN, VSXY, AEO, ANF up 3-5%) and LULU strength lack a clear driver. Barton sees specialty retail as a possible attractive Q4 long area given holiday setup, apparel trends and cheap stocks.

KO reports BMO Oct 27. JPM's Briggs Barton calls it one of the most crowded longs in Staples, models OSG +4.5% (unit case volume +2.8%, concentrate shipments +1.9%, price/mix +2.6%), and says buyside looks for ~5% organic sales.

TMT desk (Heavey): META reacted well to the $95B raise, with Mag7 trims likely making room for it. Financing is the key bottleneck in AI. VZ gave back some outperformance after dismissing a Starlink MVNO, and VZ's 10-15m 1 Gbps FWA homes target pressures cable. Flows are quiet with supply into strength across semis.

Energy desk (Henrici): silver trades at a 25% discount to its 200-day, the widest since March 2020. Managed money net length is the lowest since 1Q24, and JPM expects a ~30% (~60mln oz) fall in solar silver demand this year, moving the market toward surplus.

Refiners and cracks moved in a way the desk could not explain from headlines. Headlines leaned dovish over 24 hours (Zelensky comments on an energy ceasefire, rising Russian diesel output to 180t/day from 160t/day with consumption falling).

Pure Momentum rose 1.9% (+1z) rebounding from an MTD momentum selloff. Top baskets: China Exposure, Travel, Software, Airlines ex JBLU. Housing and Staples lagged. The 2Y auction tailed by 0.3bp and the curve flattened.
Recession L/S and Stagflation L/S baskets returned 3.4% and 1.5% last week, odd given growth data and lower breakevens and yields.

Key calendar: FOMC decision Oct 28, PCE Oct 29, ECB Oct 29, ECI Oct 30. Mag7 and big-cap earnings this week include MSFT, GOOGL (Oct 28), AMZN (Oct 29), COIN, MSTR. Political catalysts: US midterms Nov 3, US-China trade truce expiry Nov 1 (extension to Jan 20, 2027 referenced), government funding deadline Dec 11.

market_movers.rationale: JPM consumer specialist calls KO a core holding for long-only and hedge funds and one of the most crowded Staples longs. Trends were strong through the quarter, and the desk says any weakness would be gladly defended.
Stock reacted well to the $95B equity raise, with anchor interest from NVDA, AMD and AVGO. Desk calls it one of the best stories to own in tech after a big drawdown.
Gave back some Friday outperformance after the CEO was dismissive of a Starlink MVNO, with trims after earnings.
Stock added 5.2% on a sell-side upgrade.
Strength following the appointment of the former product chief to the board, which the desk calls more like window dressing than a game-changing catalyst.

sector_views.rationale: Tactically Bullish view retains a preference for Tech via pairs trades and derivatives, with a broad Tech and Cyclicals ex-Energy rally expected if the US/Iran situation moves to negotiation.
Oct 19 menu remains constructive on Financials given consumer resilience and limited direct AI exposure.
Oct 19 menu constructive on Retailers, and the consumer desk sees specialty retail as an attractive Q4 long area.
Staples lagged on the day, though KO is described as a crowded long and defensive hedge against the AI trade.

earnings_insights: KO reports BMO Oct 27. JPM's Andrea models organic sales growth (OSG) +4.5% (estimate) with unit case volumes +2.8%, concentrate shipments +1.9% and price/mix +2.6%. Buyside expects ~5% organic sales.
About a quarter of the SPX has reported, with no dips to the pre-season forecast of ~13% revenue growth, ~30% EPS growth and ~15% margins.

Earnings this week: MSFT and GOOGL after close Oct 28, AMZN, COIN and MSTR after close Oct 29, plus KO, BA, UPS, PYPL, V and others Oct 27. JPM says Mag 7 earnings need to support the sustainability of AI financing and capex.

Fed, ECB and BoJ are all expected to hold.

The UN backed Egypt's mediation alongside Pakistan and Qatar, with little sign of progress toward a deal.
Brazil general election runoff on Oct 25 triggered a ~20% EWZ decline.
Moody's kept France at Aa3 with a negative outlook.
Zelensky comments on an energy ceasefire, and Russian diesel output rising.
